transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose what brings me in is that I just keep thinking my wife and the kids would be better off if I didn't wake up. I just... lately, I've been saying I don't really need to see another winter.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not waking up?
It's been going on since my bowling partner died. That was... about a year and a month ago now.
Have you been enjoying the things you usually like to do since your bowling partner died?

No, I really haven't. I used to look forward to a lot of things... playing bridge, working out in the garden, helping with the cooking down at the church. I used to love going to Cubs games, too. But now, I just sit in my chair most of the day. I just can't seem to make myself care about any of it anymore.
Do you still find any pleasure in the things you're doing, even if it's just a little bit?

No, not even a little bit. Like I was just saying, I really just sit in my chair all day now. There's no joy left in the gardening or the bridge games or any of it. I just... I can't make myself care about them at all anymore.
Have you thought about how you would end your life if you decided to act on these thoughts?

I haven't really figured out a specific way to do it. It's more that... well, I just keep thinking my wife and the kids would be better off if I simply didn't wake up. Lately, I've just been saying to myself that I don't need to see another winter.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy level or the way you move around since your bowling partner died?

Well, yes. My wife says I move like I’m walking through deep snow these days. I just don't have the energy. Even simple things, like getting dressed in the morning or just crossing the kitchen... it takes me so long now. I usually just end up giving up before I’ve done much of anything at all.
Have you noticed any change in your weight since your bowling partner died?
I haven't really noticed. I... I don't step on the scale much these days. My clothes seem to fit about the same, I suppose, so if it has changed, I haven't paid any attention to it.
Do you feel guilty about anything in particular?

Yes. I keep going over... well, every little thing I did wrong with him. And with my family, too. I just feel like I'm no good to anybody anymore. I really believe I deserve whatever punishment is coming to me.
How long have you been feeling this way about being no good to anybody and deserving punishment?
It's been going on since he died. That was... about a year and a month ago now. Everything just sort of started feeling that way after that.
Have you been feeling restless or fidgety, or have you noticed yourself sitting still for long periods without moving?

No, I haven't been restless. It's more the opposite, really. My wife says I move like I'm walking through deep snow. Everything is just... slow. Even simple things, like getting dressed or just crossing the kitchen, it takes me so long now. I usually just end up giving up before I've really done much of anything and just sit there.
Have you been hearing voices or seeing things that other people can't?

Yes, I have. Some evenings... well, I hear his voice. Plain as day, coming from the hallway or the spare room. He tells me I should have been there, or that I failed him. My wife says the house is completely quiet, but I know what I hear.
How long have you been hearing your bowling partner's voice?

Well, it started after I got really low about his passing. Before he died, and before I sank into this whole mess, I never heard his voice. I never believed I was being punished, either. All of that... it only started after I became so down and so guilty about everything. I've never had anything like this happen during the times in my life when I felt like my usual self. It's just been since I hit this bottom.
How long have you been feeling this way, with no pleasure in activities and thoughts of not waking up?
Well, it's been going on since he passed away. That was about a year and a month ago now. Everything just sort of went dark after that, and I haven't been able to shake it since.
How many months have you been feeling this way, with no pleasure in activities and thoughts of not waking up?
Well, like I just mentioned, it's been since my bowling partner died. That was about a year and a month ago... so I suppose that makes it thirteen months now.
Has this feeling of darkness and lack of pleasure in activities been continuous since your bowling partner died, or have you had any periods where you felt somewhat better?

No, it's... it's been pretty much constant. I haven't had any days where I woke up feeling like my old self or where things felt any lighter. It's just been a steady, heavy feeling the whole time, every single day for the last thirteen months. I haven't had a break from it.
Have you had any periods, no matter how brief, where you felt even slight pleasure or interest in activities over the past thirteen months?

No, not really. I used to look forward to a lot of things... playing bridge, working in the garden, helping with the cooking down at the church. I even used to love going to Cubs games. But now, I just sit in my chair. I can't seem to make myself care about any of it anymore, not even for a little while.
Have you seen things that other people can't since your bowling partner died?

Well, I haven't seen anything, no. But... I do hear things. Some evenings, I hear his voice. It's plain as day, coming from the hallway or the spare room. He tells me I should have been there, or that I failed him. My wife says the house is quiet, that there's nothing there, but... I hear him.
Has there been any point over the last thirteen months where you felt like you were getting better, even if it was just for a short time?

No... like I mentioned a minute ago, it hasn't let up at all. There hasn't been a single day, or even an afternoon, where I thought I was turning a corner or getting better. It's just been exactly the same this whole time.
Have you had any previous episodes like this in your life before your bowling partner died?

No, never. Before my friend died and I sank into this, I never went through anything like it. I never heard his voice or believed I was being punished before... those things only started after I became so low and, well, so guilty. They haven't ever happened during any time in my life when I felt like my usual self. It all just started after he passed.
Have you ever had an episode like this before in your life?
Like I just said, no. I've never gone through anything like this before. This is the first time in my life I've ever felt this way.
